podcast.body: Following "Come Away With Me," Nora Jones' second album featured a slightly more country sound, influenced by her developing interest in bluegrass that year. Everyone in her band contributed songs to it, and it was produced by Arif Mardin and engineered by the same person who worked on her debut album. "the second album was a little more country, but everyone in the band wrote for it."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.body: This album was produced by Arif Mardin again, with Norah Jones expressing a strong desire to continue working with him and Bruce Lundvall also wanting Arif to be involved. They recorded it upstate at Alar, where Arif Mardin, known for his early departures, came up with the band and they all had fun, drinking martinis. Norah recounts a humorous moment of Arif coming downstairs in his pajamas with a martini glass for water. "I think Bruce really wanted a reef to do it. And a reef really wanted to do it. And we loved a reef. So it just, there was never any question of changing it up."
